daily.title: UN mission notes possible US war crimes in Iran strikes
daily.summary: A United Nations fact-finding mission said it found "reasonable grounds" to believe that the United States committed war crimes in two airstrikes in Iran.

daily.title: Trump hails 'major progress' in setting up US base in Poland
daily.summary: The location of the permanent US military base in Poland could be announced "very soon," Donald Trump has said. The US president also praised the leadership of his Polish counterpart, Karol Nawrocki.

daily.title: US: Trump administration weakens Endangered Species Act
daily.summary: In a recent memo, the US government would no longer consider the unintentional killing of protected wildlife as unlawful.

daily.title: Russian birth tourism to Brazil increases
daily.summary: Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and stricter regulations in Argentina, more and more Russians are choosing to travel to Brazil to give birth to children, who will obtain Brazilian nationality.

daily.title: A war-fatigued and anxious Russia picks a new parliament
daily.summary: Fuel shortages, drone strikes and mobilization rumors are fueling anxiety and war fatigue in Russia. As support for peace talks grows among Russians, the Kremlin is watching closely ahead of parliamentary elections.

daily.title: Germany: Third malaria death linked to Frankfurt Airport
daily.summary: Two new malaria cases have been registered this week near Frankfurt airport, two months after cases first emerged.

daily.title: Alexander Ovechkin backs Putin party in campaign video
daily.summary: Ice hockey legend Alexander Ovechkin has lent Vladimir Putin's party a helping hand in its parliamentary election campaign. That's in keeping with a pattern of support by an athlete who claims not to be political.

daily.title: Saudi Arabia, Houthis exchange blows as conflict escalates
daily.summary: Five people were reportedly killed as the escalation between the two sides continues to spiral. The Houthis denied attacking Mecca, with Saudi Arabia saying one person was killed by drone shrapnel.

daily.title: Judges: As AfD ascends, Germany must bolster justice system
daily.summary: German judges and prosecutors warn that the coalition needs to reform the laws covering state prosecutors to prevent "extremists in government" from abusing the legal system.

daily.title: As global crises grow, Germany cuts development aid
daily.summary: The budget of Germany's Economic Cooperation and Development Ministry is set to shrink for the fifth consecutive year. Aid organizations warn that the cuts will have severe consequences for millions of people.

daily.title: Smuggling suspected as more rare animals seen in India
daily.summary: Orangutans, rare reptiles and other exotic animals are popping up in India, suggesting the country is becoming a major destination for trafficked wildlife.

daily.title: Fact check: How disinformation fuels Houthi-Saudi conflict
daily.summary: As fighting between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia escalates, old and repurposed videos have flooded social media, with many presented as fresh footage from the front lines.

daily.title: South Africa: Police find 9th body of woman amid spree fears
daily.summary: Police in South Africa have discovered the bodies of nine women east of Johannesburg in two months, stoking fears of a serial killer or group of killers.

daily.title: Europe seeks stricter age limits for TikTok, Instagram and Facebook
daily.summary: The European Commission wants to bar children under 13 from social media platforms and curb addictive features such as infinite scrolling. Companies that fail to comply could face hefty fines.

daily.title: Klopp wants Germany's football team to 'reclaim the flag'
daily.summary: Jürgen Klopp, Germany's new head coach, says he wants his team to reclaim pride in being German after recent political developments.

daily.title: Serbian President Vucic criticizes Kosovo war crimes verdict
daily.summary: The conviction of four former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has drawn sharply different reactions across the Balkans. Serbia has accused the court of failing to fully address crimes against Serbs.

daily.title: King Charles, Earl Spencer clash over Diana death once again
daily.summary: Buckingham Palace has rejected criticism of King Charles III in a new book by the brother of his late wife, Princess Diana. Earl Charles Spencer has been a fierce critic of his former brother-in-law for decades.

daily.title: Canada's Carney welcomes associate status idea in EU speech
daily.summary: Mark Carney wants to strengthen Canada's ties to the European Union amid a growing rift with the US under Donald Trump. The US president has threatened to halt trade with Europe if it makes Canada an associate EU member.

daily.title: Jews once lived lived here: When houses tell stories
daily.summary: Time and again, residents tracing the history of their homes discover the lives of Jewish predecessors who fled or were deported amid stories of suffering and loss.

daily.title: Fiji declares HIV a national crisis, 1 in 60 adults carry it
daily.summary: Fiji's government estimates that HIV prevalence has almost tripled in the last five years. It's expanding testing, prevention and treatment services. In 2025 the tiny island recorded 16 times more new cases than in 2019.

daily.title: Jürgen Klopp's first Germany squad includes 44 players
daily.summary: Germany's new head coach Jürgen Klopp has named a huge squad for his first four games, splitting them into two groups. A host of new faces is included.

daily.title: Saint, sinner or feminist icon: How Mary Magdalene's image evolved through time
daily.summary: From "Apostle of the Apostles" to prostitute, Mary Magdalene has been assigned a wide variety of roles, as a new exhibition shows.

weekly.title: How climate change worsened Nepal's deadly mountain collapse
weekly.summary: A glacier and rock collapse in Nepal killed nearly 1,400 people and left thousands missing. Scientists say decades of warming helped set the disaster in motion.

weekly.title: UK: Village votes to 'secede' in asylum center plan protest
weekly.summary: Residents of Piddington, a tiny, remote village in Oxfordshire in England, have staged a "referendum" on leaving the UK. They are objecting to plans to open an asylum reception center at a disused military base nearby.

weekly.title: Can Canada and the EU deepen ties to counter Trump?
weekly.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is known for standing up to US President Donald Trump. Now he wants to forge a "unique alliance" with Europe. But what could such a partnership look like?

weekly.title: Chancellor Merz seeks CDU support amid far-right AfD surge
weekly.summary: Following the CDU's crushing defeat in the Saxony-Anhalt state election, many are expressing doubts about the party's leader, Chancellor Friedrich Merz. But the CDU doesn't appear to have a viable alternative.

weekly.title: Shock in Kosovo as Hague convicts former President Thaci
weekly.summary: The conviction in The Hague of former President Hashim Thaci and three former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has caused consternation in Kosovo — both among political leaders and on the streets. DW reports from Pristina.

weekly.title: British-American writer Bonnie Greer dies aged 77
weekly.summary: Chicago-born playwright Bonnie Greer, who became a familiar face in British political discourse later in life, has died. Her husband David Hutchins announced news of Greer's death.

weekly.title: After Neuer: Who will be Germany's new No. 1 goalkeeper?
weekly.summary: Following Manuel Neuer's retirement, there are many candidates to succeed him, but which goalkeeper will Jürgen Klopp choose? What factors will play a role? And will Neuer's future have an indirect influence?

weekly.title: Poland reaffirms support for Ukraine after drone strikes
weekly.summary: After Russia's recent drone attacks on targets close to the Ukraine-Poland border, Warsaw has doubled down on its support for Kyiv and pledged a "nonprovocative but serious response" to Moscow.

weekly.title: Global Gender Gap Report: Women's hard-won gains 'fragile'
weekly.summary: Two decades of progress toward gender parity is at risk as women's political representation declines, according to a new World Economic Forum report. At the current pace, the remaining gap could take 120 years to close.

weekly.title: Kosovo ex-president Thaci sentenced to 25 years for war crimes
weekly.summary: A Hague tribunal ruled that Hashim Thaci, a former leader of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA), is responsible for war crimes carried out during the war of independence with Serbia.

weekly.title: German drama 'Blindspot Berlin' revisits 2016 Christmas market attack
weekly.summary: A decade after the terrorist attack on a Berlin Christmas market, a new German miniseries looks into the institutional failures that allowed the deadly truck rampage to happen.

weekly.title: How extreme heat is hitting wallets
weekly.summary: Heat waves, wildfires and floods have cascading economic impacts, causing incomes to decline and the price of basic goods to rise. The trend will escalate as temperatures continue to increase.

weekly.title: Turkey's rights groups, EU call out LGBTQ+ crackdown
weekly.summary: Several raids and arrests of LGBTQ+ persons in Turkey have triggered sharp criticism from numerous Turkish organizations — and also from Brussels.

weekly.title: Drivers in Germany fume over soaring fuel prices
weekly.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz wants to provide relief to motorists. But exactly how this is to happen remains unclear.

weekly.title: Holocaust survivor on 'very dangerous' AfD Saxony-Anhalt win
weekly.summary: Charlotte Knobloch survived the Holocaust by passing as the daughter of non-Jewish farmers. She recently spoke with DW to express her shock following the AfD victory in Saxony-Anhalt's state election.

weekly.title: Why do authoritarian regimes target the LGBTQ+ community?
weekly.summary: A recent crackdown on the LGBTQ+ community in Turkey is symptomatic of a wider rights regression, according to experts. It's worse under authoritarian regimes, but why is it such a popular policy for these states?

weekly.title: Spanish scientists find first evidence of Diplodocus dinosaur in Europe
weekly.summary: Paleontologists in Spain say they have found the first evidence of the long-necked Diplodocus genus of dinosaur outside of North America. They found bones at the rich La Tejeria fossil site in Teruel in eastern Spain.

weekly.title: Why the era of cheap government debt is over
weekly.summary: US debt has topped $40 trillion. How risky is the country's growing debt burden. And will investors keep funding Washington's deficits?

weekly.title: Socialist Left leads far-right AfD ahead of Berlin vote
weekly.summary: The results of the Berlin election are as hard to predict as ever. Three parties are vying for first place, including the socialist Left Party and the far-right AfD. But one issue is most important to Berliners.

weekly.title: Germany news: Merz to cancel UN trip amid party infighting
weekly.summary: Germany's chancellor nixxed his trip over doubts about his leadership after party losses to the AfD in state elections. Meanwhile, Defense Minister Pistorius is in Washington for talks with his US counterpart.

weekly.title: SPD state premier campaigns as one-woman bulwark against AfD
weekly.summary: Manuela Schwesig, of the center-left SPD, has governed the state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, on the Baltic Sea coast, since 2017. Ahead of this weekend's election, she is campaigning against the nationalist AfD.

weekly.title: Netherlands: Suspected sabotage disrupts train services
weekly.summary: A major outage has hit parts of the Dutch railway system after objects were found placed across lines, authorities say. The company responsible for rail infrastructure says it suspects deliberate wrongdoing.

weekly.title: Why AI researchers warn humanity could face extinction
weekly.summary: Could artificial intelligence pose an existential threat to humanity? Some leading researchers are warning against an unregulated race toward AI superintelligence.

weekly.title: Iran and US: Two countries and the pistachio between them
weekly.summary: The pistachios sold across the United States have a surprising history: California's trees trace their roots to Iran. Now, both regions face the same threat — their farmland is sinking as groundwater disappears.

weekly.title: Europe launches two climate observation satellites
weekly.summary: The European Space Agency has put two satellites into orbit to take a closer look at the impact of climate change. One of them will focus particularly on plant life.

weekly.title: EU seeks Arctic strategy amid growing power rivalry
weekly.summary: Russia's aggression, Trump's threats against Greenland and the race for critical raw materials are pushing the Arctic to the top of Europe's agenda.

weekly.title: Ukraine, Russia set for new round of US-mediated talks
weekly.summary: New trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US could begin in October, according to Kyiv and Moscow. Few expect a breakthrough, but Ukraine is seeking a partial de-escalation to help it get through the winter.

weekly.title: Trump seeks halt to energy attacks by both Russia, Ukraine
weekly.summary: Donald Trump, under fire for record US diesel prices, claims Russia and Ukraine have agreed to stop striking energy targets. Russia said nothing; Ukraine said "we expect specifics from our partners" on any such move.

weekly.title: Women's Basketball World Cup: Can Germany harness a boom?
weekly.summary: Germany thrilled fans at the Women's Basketball World Cup. But even if this sparked a boom in the women's game, the infrastructure simply isn't ready for it.

weekly.title: Africa's richest man Dangote's IPO out of reach in Nigeria
weekly.summary: Dangote seeks $1.6 billion from investors to finance a $14.3 billion expansion and thus double the oil refinery's capacity. The offer could give millions of Nigerians a stake in the company. But who can truly afford it?

weekly.title: Far-right AfD puts pressure on German aid to Ukraine
weekly.summary: Emboldened by its win in Saxony-Anhalt, the far-right Alternative for Germany wants the government to change its Ukraine and Russia policies. Berlin is staying the course, but support is fading — especially in the east.

weekly.title: The Crusades: How a medieval holy war still shapes politics
weekly.summary: In 1095, the Catholic Church launched the Crusades: wars that left millions dead and whose legacy still shapes political and ideological conflicts.

weekly.title: EU leaders urge unity after Russian strike on train
weekly.summary: Russia's drone attack on a train near the Ukraine-Poland border has triggered EU calls to up support for Kyiv. Allies of Ukraine should show they "are not scared," said the bloc's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas.

weekly.title: Can Iran replace sea trade with land routes?
weekly.summary: Iran is shifting trade toward northern ports and land routes as its southern shipping faces a US blockade. Analysts say the corridors can keep essential goods moving, but cannot replace maritime trade.

weekly.title: In cosmopolitan Berlin, elections still closed to foreigners
weekly.summary: A quarter of Berlin residents will have no say in the German capital's city-state election because they lack citizenship. That's the highest proportion of residents excluded from the election yet, and many are unhappy.

weekly.title: Germany: Merz's CDU comes out on top in Lower Saxony polls
weekly.summary: The Christian Democrats have emerged as the strongest party following local elections in the state of Lower Saxony. The vote was closely watched as an indicator of the strength of the far-right AfD, which came in third.

weekly.title: Germany's Zverev wins US Open in golden year
weekly.summary: Alexander Zverev has won the US Open for the first time, defeating Ben Shelton in the final. It is Zverev's second Grand Slam win of 2026 after a long wait for his first title, but controversy still hangs over him.

weekly.title: Russians on the Goethe-Institut: 'Hostage to politics'
weekly.summary: Canceled language exams, disrupted plans to study in Germany and the disappearance of an important cultural link: DW users shared how the closure of Germany's Goethe-Institut in Russia has affected their lives.

weekly.title: A Romani artist in Hungary reclaims his identity
weekly.summary: Norbert Olah is an artist. He's also Romani. For a long time, he avoided making his ethnic background a theme of his art for fear of being pigeonholed. Then it became his focus.

weekly.title: Why are European banks moving gold out of United States?
weekly.summary: The Netherlands and France have moved their gold out of US vaults. Part of the reason is fears about the reliability of the US, but equally important is the need to keep gold closer to home in the event of a crisis.

weekly.title: Corals as climate archive: Are El Nino events intensifying?
weekly.summary: Records show that El Nino events have been frequent and often extreme over the past few decades. Is this normal? Or is it the result of climate change? Corals can give us a clear indication.

weekly.title: Russia's drone war comes to Moldova and Romania
weekly.summary: Incursions by Russian drones into Moldovan and Romanian airspace are increasingly common. This week the Ukrainian president's plane was stopped from taking off from Chisinau. Observers suspect the attacks are deliberate.

weekly.title: DW exclusive: Zelenskyy offers to meet Putin at G20 in Miami
weekly.summary: In an interview with DW, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country was in a strong position to negotiate and offered to meet Vladimir Putin in Miami.

weekly.title: India looks to steer BRICS away from anti-Western turn
weekly.summary: The BRICS summit 2026 takes place in Delhi this weekend. Unlike last year, Putin and Xi are expected to attend. Can India keep the expanded bloc united?

weekly.title: Turks in Germany anxious after AfD wins in Saxony-Anhalt
weekly.summary: The Alternative for Germany party's win in Saxony-Anhalt has alarmed people of Turkish origin in eastern states. Will workers and business owners abandon the increasingly AfD-friendly region for the more welcoming west?

weekly.title: The 'end of an era' as Goethe-Institut in Russia closes
weekly.summary: The Goethe-Institut was one of the last German institutions still operating in Russia. However, following Moscow's decision to close its offices, all employees will have to stop working by September 13.

weekly.title: Magyar vs. Moscow: Hungary toughens stance toward Russia
weekly.summary: Prime Minister Peter Magyar has abruptly ended the era of his predecessor's warm relations with Russia: Hungary has expelled 10 Russian diplomats. The Kremlin is considering halting gas supplies in response.

weekly.title: Germany sets its sights on Russia's shadow fleet
weekly.summary: The German government wants to follow other EU countries and take more decisive action against Russia's shadow fleet, accusing it of helping Moscow evade sanctions and carry out acts of sabotage.
